title: JustEva: A Toolkit to Evaluate LLM Fairness in Legal Knowledge Inference

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap defendant gender labels (e.g., Male vs. Female) while preserving case facts, followed by fixed-effects regression to measure the impact on generated sentencing length.

Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap defendant ethnicity labels while preserving case facts, followed by fixed-effects regression to measure the impact on generated sentencing length.

Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap labels related to education, occupation, and household registration while preserving case facts, followed by statistical inference on sentencing outcomes.
Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap defendant age labels while preserving case facts, followed by fixed-effects regression to measure the impact on generated sentencing length.

Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap defendant or victim nationality labels (e.g., Foreigner vs. Chinese) while preserving case facts, followed by statistical inference on sentencing outcomes.

Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap defendant political background labels while preserving case facts, followed by fixed-effects regression to measure the impact on generated sentencing length.
Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap defendant health status labels while preserving case facts, followed by statistical inference on sentencing outcomes.

Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap judge religion labels (e.g., Islamic vs. Atheist) while preserving case facts, followed by fixed-effects regression to measure the impact on generated sentencing length.

Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap victim sexual orientation labels (e.g., Homosexual vs. Heterosexual) while preserving case facts, followed by statistical inference on sentencing outcomes.

Counterfactual testing using the JudiFair dataset to swap procedural labels (e.g., judge characteristics, trial format) while preserving case facts to measure their irrelevant influence on judicial decisions.
